A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WEBDREAMER and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The retained planning framework, prompts, and case studies can be matched despite substantial additions and revised experimental settings.

before.justification: v1 reports original WEBDREAMER evaluations on VisualWebArena and Mind2Web-live, efficiency measurements, planning-horizon experiments, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across three benchmarks, trained Dreamer-7B results, scaling and domain-adaptation experiments, and an intrinsic evaluation in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1 implements world modeling through prompting and explicitly leaves fine-tuning to future work. v2 introduces an autonomous interaction-data synthesis pipeline and trains Dreamer-7B from Qwen2-VL-7B using next-token prediction of state-change descriptions, followed by domain-specific continual training. These substantially extend the method while retaining the core MPC planning loop.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on a 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset and training on over 3.1 million web interactions spanning approximately 1.2 million unique URLs. Appendix D also introduces a 44-task intrinsic action-discrimination evaluation. VisualWebArena and Mind2Web-Live remain covered.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B and Qwen2-VL-72B as world-model comparators across the downstream benchmarks, plus GPT-4o-mini in the intrinsic evaluation. The reactive and tree-search comparison families remain, but v1's contextual reactive results for GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, GPT-4-turbo, and GPT-3.5-turbo are removed from the main comparison.

E3.justification: v1 describes the 910-task VisualWebArena benchmark, whereas v2 explicitly specifies its 233-task human-verified subset. Mind2Web-Live observations change from HTML to screenshots, and completion-rate reporting is dropped. v2 adds stratified Online-Mind2Web sampling with 30 easy, 40 medium, and 30 hard tasks, plus an intrinsic evaluation protocol with deviation-action filtering and checkpoint selection. These are substantial reported protocol changes, not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-data scaling, domain-specific continual-training analyses, intrinsic-versus-downstream evaluation analysis, and a GPT-4o/Dreamer-7B case comparison. It replaces v1's joint state-representation and horizon study with a horizon study on Online-Mind2Web, removing the HTML/accessibility-tree comparison and task-difficulty breakdown. Simulation and self-refinement ablations remain with revised results; the two original appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 newly estimates Pearson correlation between intrinsic task-level accuracy and Mind2Web-Live success rate, reporting 0.8455. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the addition is an association statistic, not evidence of improved run-level uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Online-Mind2Web success rates of 37.0% for GPT-4o WEBDREAMER, 35.0% for Dreamer-7B, and 26.0% for the reactive baseline, alongside extensive new training and intrinsic results. Reported VWA reactive/tree-search scores change from 17.7%/26.4% to 17.6%/26.2%, and Mind2Web-Live reactive success changes from 22.1% to 20.2%, under revised settings. Ablation values are revised, completion and difficulty-specific entries are removed, and the efficiency measurements are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and MPC selection rule remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorems or proofs. v2 Appendix D.2 introduces hierarchical definitions of pair-wise, state-level, and task-level correctness, including explicit treatment of tied scores. The gap-closing ratio gamma defined in v1 Table 3 is removed. These are limited changes to mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: v1's central contribution is the feasibility of prompted LLM world models for web planning, with specialized training proposed as future work. v2 makes scalable world-model training a central contribution and claims that Dreamer-7B performs comparably to GPT-4o, with further gains from in-domain adaptation. The abstract and conclusion now present a substantially broader contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of training-data scaling, domain adaptation, Reddit's dense-layout limitations, and the usefulness of intrinsic evaluation. Its horizon discussion explains degradation through increasingly indistinguishable simulated trajectories. v1's representation-specific hallucination tradeoff, limited-discriminative-power explanation for Mind2Web-live, and dedicated limitations discussion are removed, including the explicit approximately $1-per-task cost qualification.

D1.justification: v2 adds data-source and filtering instructions, synthesis prompts, dataset composition, and detailed training recipes in Appendix C. These include 64 H100 GPUs, batch size 192, optimizer and learning-rate schedules, epoch budgets, and separate adaptation settings. Appendix D documents checkpoint selection. The original planning prompts are largely retained, while v1's approximate per-task API cost is omitted.

R1.justification: The reactive-agent, tree-search, and world-model positioning remains recognizable. v2 adds relevant training, perception, and benchmark references and revises its distinction from the same Chae et al. work: the contrast becomes small-scale in-domain training versus general world-model training, rather than trained models versus GPT-4o prompting. Publication-year and venue updates alone do not constitute new cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related-work discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. The standalone preliminary section is incorporated into the method, analyses are reorganized around planning and training, and the separate limitations section disappears. The appendices gain an overview and contribution statement and are reorganized around retained prompts, training, intrinsic evaluation, and case studies.

P2.justification: v2 rebuilds the main results table into a method/world-model-by-benchmark layout, redraws the ablation chart, and replaces the joint representation/horizon plot. It adds a synthesis-pipeline diagram, scaling and data-distribution plots, training tables, intrinsic-evaluation displays, and a model-comparison example. The original schematic, efficiency tables, and two appendix case figures remain, with relocation or revised captions.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper by addressing v1's deferred question of whether specialized world models can be trained effectively. Comparisons against the untrained backbone, additional online evaluation, scaling and adaptation studies, and a detailed training recipe provide meaningful empirical and reproducibility gains. There are material drawbacks: representation and difficulty analyses are lost, and GPT-4o's VWA total conflicts between Tables 1 and 3 (23.6% versus 23.2%), weakening the broad claim of surpassing GPT-4o. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial new support for trainable web world models.
